description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting the reading and writing of iCalendar files.  Includes:
- Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar), RFC 5545
- Parameter Value Encoding in iCalendar and vCard, RFC 6868
- New Properties for iCalendar, RFC 7986
- jCal: The JSON Format for iCalendar, RFC 7265
- xCal: The XML Format for iCalendar, RFC 6321
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- The packages no longer have a `net8.0` build. An application on .NET 8 or .NET 9 gets a .NET Standard build, without the APIs that only the `net10.0` build has, such as `DateOnly` and `TimeOnly` support. To keep those APIs, move the application to .NET 10.
- The `netstandard1.x` and `netstandard2.0` builds no longer list `JetBrains.Annotations` as a NuGet dependency. If your code uses its attributes and you got the package through DataStandardizer, add a reference to `JetBrains.Annotations` to your project.
- `IcalReader`, `XcalReader`, `JcalReader` and their writers reject a `FMTTYPE` parameter that isn't one type and subtype (RFC 5545 §3.2.8), or that appears twice. Set `IcalOptions.AllowInvalidValues` to accept it.
- `IcalReader`, `XcalReader`, `JcalReader` and their writers reject a parameter defined with one value that has more, such as `CN=Doe, John`, and a parameter repeated on a property RFC 5545 or RFC 7986 defines. Set `IcalOptions.AllowInvalidValues` to accept them.
- `default(TzDataTimezone)` is `Etc/UTC`, equal to the new `TzDataTimezone.Etc.UTC` field: it converts to `"Etc/UTC"` instead of `null`, `ToString()` returns `"UTC"`, and its members return the zone lines, location and offsets of `Etc/UTC` instead of throwing `InvalidOperationException`.
- `IcalReader` and `IcalContentLineReader` reject a last content line that doesn't end with CRLF, as RFC 5545 §3.1 requires. Set the new `IcalOptions.AcceptMissingFinalLineBreak` to accept it.
- `IcalReader` and `IcalContentLineReader` reject a byte order mark at the start of the data (RFC 5545 §3.6), and a byte order mark no longer selects UTF-16 or UTF-32. Set the new `IcalOptions.AcceptByteOrderMark` to skip it, and `IcalOptions.Encoding` to read data that isn't UTF-8.
- `IcalReader` and `IcalContentLineReader` throw `IcalFileException` for data that isn't valid UTF-8 (RFC 5545 §3.1.4), instead of replacing it with U+FFFD, and can't read on after it. Set `IcalOptions.Encoding` to `Encoding.UTF8` to replace it.
- `JcalWriter` and `XcalWriter` refuse further writes, with `InvalidOperationException`, after a write to their stream or XML writer, or a flush of it, fails, rather than going on to write a document that isn't valid jCal or xCal. A calendar refused before any of it is written still leaves the writer able to continue.

New:
- `IcalContentLine.GetFormatType` and `IcalContentLineView.GetFormatType` read the FMTTYPE parameter (RFC 5545 §3.2.8) as a `MimeMediaType`.
- `TzDataTimezone.Parse`, `TryParse` and the explicit conversion accept `Etc/UTC` and the deprecated names linked to it, such as `UTC` and `Zulu`.
- `IcalTimeZoneResolver.TzData` resolves the TZIDs `Etc/UTC`, `UTC`, `Zulu` and the other names the TZ Database links to `Etc/UTC`, with an offset of 0.
- `IcalOptions.AllowQuotedParameterValues` accepts a quoted value for a parameter whose grammar has no quoted form, reported as the new `IcalDiagnosticKind.QuotedParameterValue`.

Fixed:
- Debuggers can step into the packages' source through Source Link.
- `MaxLineLength` also limits the folds in a content line, so a line with more folds than the limit is rejected as too long.
- `TzDataTimezone.CompareTo` orders time zones by identifier instead of throwing `ArgumentException`.
- `IcalReader` rejects, and `IcalWriter` refuses to write, a parameter value in double quotes where the parameter's grammar has no quoted form, such as `FMTTYPE="audio/basic"` (RFC 5545 §3.2.8).
- `IcalContentLineReader` and `IcalReader` can't read on after their `TextReader` or `Stream` throws, instead of joining the characters on either side of the failure into one line.
- IcalContentLineReader throws ObjectDisposedException for a read disposed while it completes from the buffer.
- `IcalContentLineWriter.WriteLineAsync` completes with `ObjectDisposedException` when the writer is disposed during a write that completes without waiting, and no longer does synchronous I/O when releasing it.
- `IcalContentLineWriter.WriteLinesAsync` cancels when given no lines and a canceled token.
- `IcalContentLineWriter.WriteLineAsync` faults its task, rather than canceling it, when the writer is disposed during a write whose text writer throws an `OperationCanceledException` whose token isn't canceled.
- `IcalContentLineWriter`'s asynchronous methods, and `DisposeAsync`, fault their task, rather than canceling it, when the underlying text writer or stream throws an `OperationCanceledException` while the caller's token isn't canceled, and the writer can continue after it.
- `IcalContentLineWriter.WriteLineAsync` cancels its task when the caller's token is canceled and the text writer throws an `OperationCanceledException` that carries another token, or none.
- IcalWriter, JcalWriter, XcalWriter and IcalContentLineReader cancel an asynchronous operation only when the caller's token is canceled.
- IcalReader, JcalReader and XcalReader cancel an asynchronous read only when the caller's token is canceled.
- XcalReader and XcardReader no longer overflow the stack on .NET Framework when their source fails a read with an OperationCanceledException.
- IcalTimeZoneRules.ToUtc throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, as documented, for a local time whose instant falls before year 1 or after year 9999.
- IcalTimeZoneRules.ToUtc throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a time in an overlap whose first occurrence falls before year 1, instead of returning the second occurrence.
- IcalEvent.GetOccurrences throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, not a wrong end time, for a nominal duration of more days than the range of dates holds.
- XcalReader.ReadCalendar throws IcalFileException, not XmlException, for malformed XML in the text of an element.
- `XcalReader` throws `IcalFileException`, not `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, for an XML declaration with a garbled encoding name on .NET 10.
- reading a calendar with a very long TZID that starts with a solidus no longer takes time quadratic in its length.

Changed:
- The netstandard1.x and netstandard2.0 builds now carry nullable annotations, so projects on C# 8 or later with nullable enabled get null warnings from them.
- The package now depends on `DataStandardizer.Communication`, for media types and base64.
- `IcalTimeZone.FromTzData` defines `Etc/UTC` for `default(TzDataTimezone)` instead of throwing `InvalidOperationException`.
- IcalReader, XcalReader and JcalReader accept at most 64 levels of nested components; deeper nesting throws IcalFileException.
